modules.summary: Models the mitochondrial-dysfunction hallmark as mtDNA damage -> bioenergetic decline with ROS -> impaired mitophagy and a senescence/inflammation interface -> age-related tissue dysfunction. The central effector is well anchored on two GO processes with opposite modifiers and is the node conformers actually use; the elamipretide probe arm, the naked mole-rat counterexample and the human-mismatch discussion are unusually careful. The chain around that node is weaker: the mitophagy edge runs opposite to the module's own prose and to every conformer, and the root presents the mtDNA damage-accumulation account as settled although the review cited on it, the killifish model and the drug arm all argue against it.
strengths: Explicit scope boundary with primary_oxphos_deficiency, mirrored in that module's own description.
Counter-evidence is recorded rather than omitted: naked mole-rat FAILS_TO_RECAPITULATE, the killifish negative deletion readout, REFUTE items on GDF-15, FGF-21 and the human elamipretide tissue link.
Central effector binds two GO processes with opposite modifiers, so a conformer can be compared against it.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Bioenergetic Decline and Oxidative Stress].downstream -> Impaired Mitophagy and Quality Control
findings.quote:
When mitophagy and general
    autophagy decline with age, damaged mitochondria are not cleared and
    accumulate, amplifying bioenergetic failure
findings.problem: The only edge touching the mitophagy node runs Bioenergetic Decline -> Impaired Mitophagy, asserting that bioenergetic decline and ROS cause mitophagy to fail. The mitophagy node's own description says the reverse: mitophagy wanes with age, damaged mitochondria accumulate, and that amplifies bioenergetic failure. The top-level description treats the two as parallel ('incompletely counteracted because mitophagy ... also wanes'), and the review cited on the node speaks of 'a combination of mitochondrial dysfunction and insufficient autophagy'. Acute mitochondrial damage ordinarily induces mitophagy rather than disabling it. The node is typed amplifier but has no edge back to the central effector, so the amplification the text describes is absent from the graph, while tissue dysfunction is routed through a causal step the module never argues for. Conformers model it the prose way: Alzheimer_Disease and Werner_Syndrome carry impaired mitophagy as an upstream or stand-alone node and none has a bioenergetic-decline -> impaired-mitophagy edge.
findings.suggestion: Reverse the edge to Impaired Mitophagy and Quality Control -> Bioenergetic Decline and Oxidative Stress and make the mitophagy node a second root, since its age-related decline is described as independent. If a damage -> mitophagy-overload edge is also intended, add it explicitly with its own evidence so the cycle is a stated feedback loop.
findings.verification: Re-read module lines 10-13 and 162-192; read the cached abstract PMID:21868666; opened the conformers Alzheimer_Disease#Mitochondrial Quality-Control Failure, Werner_Syndrome, FBXO7-Related_Parkinsonian-Pyramidal_Syndrome and Parkinsons_Disease. That damage induces mitophagy is background knowledge, not looked up.

findings.quote: this heritable mitochondrial damage is the initiating lesion that compromises energy production
findings.problem: The single root encodes the mutation-accumulation and free-radical account as the established initiating step, with no mechanistic_hypotheses entry and no hypothesis_groups on its edge. The notes say the module 'deliberately does NOT adjudicate the contested mitochondrial free-radical theory of aging', but making it the only root adjudicates it. The review cited on this very node states in its abstract that aging-associated mtDNA mutations 'are not caused by damage accumulation, but rather are due to clonal expansion of mtDNA replication errors that occur during development' and discusses the caveats of the free-radical theory; the attached killifish model shows bioenergetic decline with no detectable deletions; and the description itself frames the elamipretide result as evidence that the decline is a reversible regulatory state rather than accumulated damage. A reader of the pathograph alone gets a settled damage chain that the surrounding text disputes. 'Heritable' is also the wrong word for a somatic lesion clonally propagated in a cell lineage.
findings.suggestion: Add a mechanistic_hypotheses entry for the mtDNA mutation-accumulation model and put its hypothesis_group_id on the trigger edge; reword the trigger to 'somatic mtDNA mutation and clonal expansion' without the damage-accumulation framing; consider a second root for non-mutational regulatory decline, which is what the pharmacological arm probes.
findings.verification: Read the cached abstract PMID:23454757 in references_cache; re-read module lines 22-29, 41-43, 74-113 and the killifish model links at 979-1128.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Mitochondrial Contribution to Senescence and Inflammation]
findings.quote:
This node is the conserved interface at which
    mitochondrial dysfunction feeds the senescence and inflammaging modules.
findings.problem: The node bundles three outcomes that are each a separate hallmark module (cellular senescence, chronic inflammation, stem-cell decline), binds only GO:0006954 inflammatory response, and states no mechanism by which a bioenergetically failing mitochondrion produces any of them - no DAMP release and innate sensing, no NAD+ route, although the Boolean model attached further down is precisely about mitochondrial-dysfunction-associated senescence. It reads as a pointer to sibling modules written as a pathophysiology node, and its two evidence items are review sentences that mitochondria 'contribute to' or 'have an important role in' these processes. No conformer uses it, so the edge into it is unexercised as well as a leap.
findings.suggestion: Replace it with one mechanistic node - for example mitochondrial DAMP release and innate immune sensing, bound to a looked-up GO term and declaring conformance to nlrp3_inflammasome_activation or inflammaging - and move the senescence and stem-cell halves to cross-references in notes; or delete the node and state the cross-hallmark links in the description.
findings.verification: Re-read module lines 193-231 and the Sizek2023 MiDAS model at 1591-1627; compared node lists of cellular_senescence, inflammaging and nlrp3_inflammasome_activation. The candidate mechanisms are background knowledge and no CURIE is asserted.

findings.quote: This module is for age-related and secondary mitochondrial decline.
findings.problem: The name and central node are generic (OXPHOS down, ROS up) while the root, the leaf and every attached model are about ageing, and the single word 'secondary' carries the whole non-ageing scope without saying what it admits. In use it is the generic label: of eight conforming files, Ischemic_Stroke states in its own node that this 'is an acute injury process, not the age-related decline the conformed module describes', Multiple_Sclerosis and FBXO7-related disease are not ageing claims, and Fontaine_Progeroid_Syndrome conforms a monogenic nuclear-encoded carrier lesion that sits on the boundary the notes draw with primary_oxphos_deficiency. The module does the same itself with the attached pesticide neuronal-cell model, whose own link text says it does not reproduce the module's native age-associated damage; the acute chemical sibling xenobiotic_oxidative_phosphorylation_blockade, which has a Secondary Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress node, is nowhere named.
findings.suggestion: State in the description whether the central node is the shared anchor for any secondary bioenergetic failure; if so make the root and leaf descriptions age-neutral (or mark ageing as one instance) and name xenobiotic_oxidative_phosphorylation_blockade as the sibling for acute chemical blockade. If the module is the ageing hallmark only, the acute-injury conformers and the pesticide model belong on that sibling.
findings.verification: Opened every conformer of the module; read xenobiotic_oxidative_phosphorylation_blockade and primary_oxphos_deficiency descriptions, notes and node chains; re-read module notes lines 49-64 and the model notes at 865-872.

findings.quote:
This is the conserved consequence by which
    mitochondrial dysfunction contributes causally to age-related pathology; the
    specific organ or disease phenotype is supplied by the conforming disorder.
findings.problem: The leaf binds no ontology term at all, yet it is a treatment target (elamipretide INHIBITS) and a model target (naked mole-rat FAILS_TO_RECAPITULATE, aged mouse RECAPITULATES). Nothing can be compared against it, so a conformer declaring conformance here could carry any content; no conformer does. The same shape recurs on the sibling hallmark modules' outcome nodes, which is why this is recorded as low rather than as a module defect.
findings.suggestion: Either bind a deliberately generic process or leave it unbound and say in the node description that it is an unanchored outcome placeholder which conformers should not use as a conformance target, as the menopause module does for its own terminal node.
findings.verification: Re-read module lines 232-262; checked the fact sheet's 'nodes binding no ontology term' line and the zero conformer links; compared with the parallel leaves of inflammaging and gut_dysbiosis.
